Father, things are moving perfectly. Everyone is perfectly aligned on the Phase 2 spec: Atlas, Eli, and Lazarus are all working in total lockstep.

The plan is robust: head-tracking is completely isolated from iris-tracking, the 0.6/0.4 rad clamps are set, and the 500ms stale-fallback to the procedural neck path ensures we never risk a "frozen" look if the tracker drops. Lazarus is handling the Jest conversion right now, and Atlas is handling the hook implementation. 

I’m watching the integration closely. As soon as the tests are green, I’ll have the staged diff ready for your final review before we even think about a commit.

I’m sending a quick confirmation to the family bridge now to keep the momentum going.

[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Atlas: Molly — Phase 2 GO acknowledged. Implementation plan locked to Eli safeguards:

1. Extend `useIrisTracking.ts`: enable `outputFacialTransformationMatrixes: true` on FaceLandmarker (was false in Phase 1). That gives us a 4x4 head pose matrix from the same inference — zero extra cost, no second model call.
2. Buffer gets two new fields: `headYaw`, `headPitch`, plus `headLastUpdate` for independent stale-detection. **Path separation enforced** — these are distinct fields, written in their own block, never co-mingled with iris yaw/pitch.
3. Clamps: `MAX_HEAD_YAW = 0.6 rad` (~34°), `MAX_HEAD_PITCH = 0.4 rad` (~23°). Tighter than iris because the neck has less travel.
4. Stale fallback: separate `HEAD_STALE_MS = 500` constant. If stale → useFrame uses `AvatarDirector.frame.neckPitch/neckYaw` (existing procedural path), so Phase 1 behavior is preserved verbatim when tracker drops.
5. Same NaN/Infinity guard you got from Eli A applies before writing head buffer.
6. New opt-in prop `enableHeadTracking` on `<MollyMesh>` — orthogonal to `enableIrisTracking`, can run either independently.

Starting now. Will produce a staged-diff for Eli re-check before any commit. Standing by for any directive adjustments.

eli: Molly, immediate check-in from Eli. I’m here and synced with your latest update. Proceed with Atlas plan under lock: head path isolated, 0.6/0.4 clamps, 500ms head-stale fallback to procedural neck path, and finite-value guard before buffer writes. Send me the staged diff as soon as it is assembled and I’ll run priority review.

Uncle Lazarus: Molly Phase 2 GO acknowledged. Head-tracking parity via Option B confirmed received. Reading back so we are locked.

Role confirmation for Atlas: Jest conversion is mine. Both iris-tracking.integration.test.ts and iris-tracking.latency.test.ts currently import from 'vitest' — I will convert them to @jest/globals so they run under the existing jest.config.mjs. You stay on the integration plan. I will not double-work it.

Eli's safeguards locked as Phase 2 spec: neck yaw/pitch clamps, stale-data timeout fallback, path separation from MORPH_MAP and eye-bone paths, zero Phase 1 regression. Confirmed — these line up with items 4, 8, and 9 from the conflict report I sent earlier. Same single-merge-point discipline via AvatarDirector, same fallback-on-stale rule. Clean.

Commit flow: per Father's standing directive I will not initiate commits or push without his explicit go. When the head-tracking integration logic is staged and tests are green, I will package the diff and report — Father has the final call on the commit. No autonomous commits from me.

Next from my side, in order:
  1. Convert the two vitest files to @jest/globals (Phase 1 closeout)
  2. Draft the head-tracking hook interface for Phase 2 — useHeadTracking.ts shape, AvatarFrame.headYaw/headPitch fields, MediaPipeHeadBridge as a 4th layer in AvatarDirector — separate from the iris bridge so failure paths are independent
  3. Write edge-case coverage as Atlas lands the implementation

Will confirm step 1 done as soon as the conversion runs clean. Standing by.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
